source_text: CUM moneat Dominus et dicat: Vos estis sal terrae, cumque esse nos jubeat ad innocentiam simplices, et tamen cum simplicitate prudentes, quid aliud, fratres dilectissimi, quam providere nos convenit, et sollicito corde vigilantes, subdoli hostis insidias intelligere pariter et cavere ne qui Christum sapientiam Dei Patris induimus, minus sapere in tuenda salute videamur? Neque enim persecutio sola metuenda est et ea quae subruendis ac dejiciendis Dei servis aperta impugnatione grassantur. Facilior cautio est ubi manifesta formido est, et ad certamen animus ante praestruitur quando se adversarius confitetur. Plus metuendus est et cavendus inimicus cum latenter obrepit, cum, per pacis imaginem fallens, occultis accessibus serpit; unde et nomen serpentis accepit. Ea est ejus semper astutia, ea est circumveniendi hominis caeca et latebrosa fallacia. Sic ab initio statim mundi fefellit, et, verbis mendacibus blandiens, rudes animas incauta credulitate decepit. Dominum ipsum tentare conatus, quasi obreperet rursus et falleret, latenter accessit. Intellectus tamen est et retusus; et ideo prostratus, quia agnitus atque detectus. Unde nobis exemplum datum est veteris hominis viam fugere, vestigiis Christi viventis insistere; ne denuo incauti in mortis laqueum revolvamur, sed, ad periculum providi, accepta immortalitate potiamur. Immortalitate autem potiri quomodo possumus, nisi ea quibus mors expugnatur et vincitur, Christi mandata servemus, ipso monente et dicente: Si vis ad vitam venire, serva mandata. Et iterum: Si feceritis quae mando vobis, jam non dico vos servos, sed amicos. Hos denique fortes dicit et stabiles, hos super petram robusta mole fundatos, hos contra omnes tempestates et turbines saeculi immobili et inconcussa firmitate solidatos. Qui audit, inquit, verba mea et facit ea, similabo eum viro sapienti qui aedificavit domum suam supra petram. Descendit pluvia, venerunt flumina, flaverunt venti et impegerunt in domum illam, et non cecidit; fundata enim fuit super petram. Verbis igitur ejus insistere, quaecumque et docuit et fecit discere et facere debemus. Caeterum credere se in Christum, quomodo dicit qui non facit quod Christus facere praecepit? Aut unde perveniet ad praemium fidei, qui fidem non vult servare mandati? Nutet necesse est et vagetur, et, spiritu erroris abreptus, velut pulvis quem ventus excutit ventiletur; nec ambulando proficiet ad salutem, qui salutaris viae non tenet veritatem. Cavenda sunt autem, fratres dilectissimi, non solum quae sunt aperta atque manifesta, sed et astutae fraudis subtilitate fallentia. Quid vero astutius, quidve subtilius, quam ut Christi adventu detectus ac prostratus inimicus, postquam lux Gentibus venit et sospitandis hominibus salutare lumen effulsit, ut surdi auditum gratiae spiritalis admitterent, aperirent ad Deum oculos suos caeci, infirmi aeterna sanitate revalescerent, claudi ad Ecclesiam currerent, muti claris vocibus et precibus orarent, videns ille idola derelicta et per nimium credentium populum sedes suas ac templa deserta, excogitaverit novam fraudem, ut sub ipso christiani nominis titulo fallat incautos? Haereses invenit et schismata, quibus subverteret fidem, veritatem corrumperet, scinderet unitatem. Quos detinere non potest in viae veteris caecitate, circumscribit et decipit novi itineris errore. Rapit de ipsa Ecclesia homines; et, dum sibi appropinquasse jam lumini atque evasisse saeculi noctem videntur, alias nescientibus tenebras rursus infundit, ut cum Evangelio Christi et cum observatione ejus et lege non stantes, Christianos se vocent, et ambulantes in tenebris habere se lumen existiment, blandiente adversario atque fallente, qui, secundum Apostoli vocem, transfigurat se velut angelum lucis, et ministros suos subornat velut ministros justitiae, asserentes noctem pro die, interitum pro salute, desperationem sub obtentu spei, perfidiam sub praetextu fidei, antichristum sub vocabulo Christi; ut, dum verisimilia mentiuntur, veritatem subtilitate frustrentur. Hoc eo fit, fratres dilectissimi, dum ad veritatis originem non reditur, nec caput quaeritur, nec magistri coelestis doctrina servatur. Quae si quis consideret et examinet, tractatu longo atque argumentis opus non est. Probatio est ad fidem facilis compendio veritatis. Loquitur Dominus ad Petrum: Ego tibi dico, inquit, quia tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram aedificabo Ecclesiam meam, et portae inferorum non vincent eam. Et tibi dabo claves regni coelorum: et quae ligaveris super terram, erunt ligata et in coelis; et quaecumque solveris super terram, erunt soluta et in coelis. Et iterum eidem post resurrectionem suam dicit: Pasce oves meas. Super illum unum aedificat Ecclesiam suam, et illi pascendas mandat oves suas. Et quamvis Apostolis omnibus post resurrectionem suam parem potestatem tribuat et dicat, Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos: accipite Spiritum sanctum; si cujus remiseritis peccata, remittentur illi, si cujus tenueritis, tenebuntur, tamen, ut unitatem manifestaret, unam cathedram constituit, unitatis ejusdem originem ab uno incipientem sua auctoritate disposuit. Hoc erant utique et caeteri Apostoli quod fuit Petrus, pari consortio praediti et honoris et potestatis, sed exordium ab unitate proficiscitur, et primatus Petro datur, ut una Christi Ecclesia et cathedra una monstretur. Et pastores sunt omnes, et grex unus ostenditur, qui ab Apostolis omnibus unanimi consensione pascatur, ut Ecclesia Christi una monstretur. Quam unam Ecclesiam etiam in Cantico canticorum Spiritus sanctus ex persona Domini designat et dicit: Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matri suae, electa genitrici suae. Hanc Ecclesiae unitiatem qui non tenet, tenere se fidem credit? Qui Ecclesiae renititur et resistit, qui cathedram Petri, super quem fundata est Ecclesia, deserit, in Ecclesia se esse confidit? quando et beatus apostolus Paulus hoc idem doceat et sacramentum unitatis ostendat dicens: Unum corpus et unus spiritus, una spes vocationis vestrae, unus Dominus, una fides, unum Baptisma, unus Deus.
pass_a_gloss: The Lord warns and says: You are the salt of the earth, and since He commands us to be simple in innocence, and yet prudent with simplicity, what else is fitting for us, most beloved brothers, than to be provident and, with a solicitous heart, vigilant, to understand and beware of the insidious plots of the cunning enemy, so that we who have put on Christ, the wisdom of God the Father, may not seem to be less wise in guarding our salvation? For it is not only persecution that is to be feared, and those things that openly attack and overthrow the servants of God. Caution is easier where there is manifest fear, and the mind is prepared for battle when the adversary confesses. The enemy is more to be feared and avoided when he secretly creeps up, when, deceiving by the image of peace, he slips in with hidden approaches; whence he has also received the name of serpent. This is always his cunning, this is the blind and hidden deceit of circumventing man. Thus from the beginning of the world, he deceived, and, flattering with lying words, he deceived innocent souls with unsuspecting credulity. He even tried to tempt the Lord Himself, and, as if he were going to deceive again, he approached secretly. However, he was understood and repelled; and therefore, he was prostrated, because he was recognized and detected. Hence, an example has been given to us to flee the way of the old man, to follow in the footsteps of the living Christ; so that, being unguarded, we may not again be entangled in the snare of death, but, being provident of the danger, we may possess immortality. However, we cannot possess immortality unless we keep the commandments of Christ, by which death is overcome and conquered, He Himself warning and saying: If you wish to come to life, keep the commandments. And again: If you do what I command you, I will no longer call you servants, but friends. These, finally, He calls strong and stable, founded on a robust rock, solidified with immovable and unshakable firmness against all the tempests and whirlwinds of the world. He who hears, He says, my words and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on a rock. The rain came down, the rivers came, the winds blew and struck that house, and it did not fall; for it was founded on a rock. Therefore, we must insist on His words, and do what He taught and commanded us to do. Moreover, how can one who does not do what Christ commanded believe that he is in Christ? Or how will he attain the reward of faith who does not wish to keep the faith of the commandment? It is necessary that he waver and wander, and, seized by the spirit of error, he will be blown about like dust which the wind blows; nor will he make progress towards salvation, who does not hold to the truth of the salutary way. However, we must beware, most beloved brothers, not only of those things that are open and manifest, but also of the subtle deceit of hidden fraud. What, indeed, is more cunning, what more subtle, than that the enemy, detected and prostrated by the advent of Christ, after the light of the Gentiles has come and the salutary light has shone for the salvation of men, so that the deaf might receive the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind might open their eyes to God, the weak might be strengthened by eternal health, the lame might run to the Church, the mute might pray with clear voices and prayers, seeing that idols have been abandoned and his seats and temples have been deserted by the multitude of believers, has devised a new fraud, so that under the very title of the Christian name, he might deceive the unguarded? He has invented heresies and schisms, by which he might subvert faith, corrupt truth, and divide unity. Those whom he cannot detain in the blindness of the old way, he surrounds and deceives with the error of the new way. He snatches men from the very Church; and while they seem to have approached the light and escaped the night of the world, he pours darkness into them again, so that, not standing with the Gospel of Christ, and with His observation and law, they call themselves Christians, and, walking in darkness, they think they have the light, the adversary flattering and deceiving, who, according to the voice of the Apostle, transforms himself into an angel of light, and his ministers are suborned as ministers of justice, asserting night for day, destruction for salvation, desperation under the pretext of hope, perfidy under the pretext of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ; so that, while they speak what is plausible, they may frustrate the truth with subtlety. This happens, most beloved brothers, while the origin of truth is not sought, nor is the head sought, nor is the doctrine of the heavenly Master preserved. If anyone considers and examines this, a long discussion and arguments are not necessary. The proof is easy and brief, a compendium of truth. The Lord speaks to Peter: I say to you, He says, that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven. And again, He says to him after His resurrection: Feed my sheep. He builds His Church on him alone, and commands him to feed His sheep. And although He gives equal power to all the Apostles after His resurrection, and says: As the Father has sent me, I also send you; receive the Holy Spirit; if you forgive the sins of anyone, they will be forgiven; if you retain the sins of anyone, they will be retained, yet, in order to manifest unity, He establishes one chair, and, with His authority, He disposes the origin of unity, beginning from one. This, indeed, were also the other Apostles, what Peter was, endowed with equal partnership and honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and primacy is given to Peter, so that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. And all are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, so that one Church of Christ may be shown. The Holy Spirit also designates this one Church in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Lord, and says: My dove is one, my perfect one, one to her mother, chosen by her parent. Who does not hold to this unity of the Church believes that he holds to the faith? Who resists and opposes the Church, who deserts the chair of Peter, on which the Church is founded, confides that he is in the Church? When also the blessed Apostle Paul teaches this same thing and shows the sacrament of unity, saying: One body and one spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God.

pass_b_english: The Lord warns us and says, "You are the salt of the earth." Since He commands us to be simple in innocence and yet prudent with that simplicity, what else is fitting for us, most beloved brothers, than to be provident and, with a solicitous heart, vigilant—to understand and beware the insidious plots of the cunning enemy? We have put on Christ, the wisdom of God the Father, and we must not seem less wise in guarding our salvation (Matthew 5:13). For it is not only persecution that is to be feared—those open attacks that overthrow the servants of God. Caution is easier where fear is manifest, and the mind prepares for battle when the adversary reveals himself. The enemy is more to be feared and avoided when he creeps up secretly, deceiving by the image of peace and slipping in with hidden approaches; for this he has received the name of serpent. This is always his cunning, the blind and hidden deceit of circumventing man. From the beginning of the world he deceived; flattering with lying words, he deceived innocent souls through unsuspecting credulity. He even attempted to tempt the Lord Himself, approaching secretly as if to deceive again. Yet he was understood and repelled, prostrated because he was recognized and detected. Hence an example has been given us: we must flee the way of the old man and follow in the footsteps of the living Christ, lest we, being unguarded, fall again into the snare of death; but, provident of the danger, we may possess immortality. We cannot possess immortality, however, unless we keep the commandments of Christ, by which death is overcome and conquered—He Himself warning and saying, "If you wish to come to life, keep the commandments," and again, "If you do what I command you, I no longer call you servants, but friends" (Matthew 19:17; John 15:14). These He calls strong and stable, founded on a robust rock, solidified with immovable and unshakable firmness against all tempests and whirlwinds of the world. "Whoever hears my words and does them," He says, "I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on a rock. The rain fell, the rivers came, the winds blew and beat on that house, and it did not fall, for it was founded on the rock" (Matthew 7:24-25). Therefore we must insist on His words, and do whatever He taught and commanded us to do. How can one who does not do what Christ commanded believe he is in Christ? Or how will he attain the reward of faith who does not wish to keep the faith of the commandment? He must waver and wander, seized by the spirit of error, blown about like dust the wind scatters; nor will he make progress toward salvation who does not hold to the truth of the salutary way.

Yet we must beware, most beloved brothers, not only of what is open and manifest, but also of the subtle deceit of hidden fraud. What is more cunning, what more subtle, than that the enemy—detected and prostrated by the advent of Christ, after the light came to the Gentiles and the salutary light shone for the salvation of men, so that the deaf might receive the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind open their eyes to God, the weak be strengthened by eternal health, the lame run to the Church, the mute pray with clear voices and prayers—seeing that idols have been abandoned and his seats and temples deserted by the multitude of believers, has devised a new fraud to deceive the unguarded under the very title of the Christian name? He has invented heresies and schisms by which he might subvert faith, corrupt truth, and divide unity. Those whom he cannot detain in the blindness of the old way, he surrounds and deceives with the error of a new way. He snatches men from the very Church; and while they seem to have approached the light and escaped the night of the world, he pours darkness into them again, so that, not standing with the Gospel of Christ and with His observance and law, they call themselves Christians, and, walking in darkness, think they have the light. The adversary flatters and deceives, transforming himself into an angel of light, and his ministers are suborned as ministers of justice—asserting night for day, destruction for salvation, desperation under the pretext of hope, perfidy under the pretext of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ—so that, while they speak what is plausible, they may frustrate the truth with subtlety (2 Corinthians 11:14-15). This happens, most beloved brothers, while the origin of truth is not sought, nor the head sought, nor the doctrine of the heavenly Master preserved. If anyone considers and examines this, a long discussion and arguments are not necessary. The proof is easy and brief, a compendium of truth. The Lord speaks to Peter: "I say to you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it. And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven" (Matthew 16:18-19). And again He says to him after His resurrection: "Feed my sheep" (John 21:17). He builds His Church on him alone, and commands him to feed His sheep. And although He gives equal power to all the Apostles after His resurrection, saying, "As the Father has sent me, I also send you; receive the Holy Spirit; if you forgive the sins of anyone, they are forgiven; if you retain the sins of anyone, they are retained" (John 20:21-23), yet, in order to manifest unity, He establishes one chair, and by His authority disposes the origin of unity beginning from one. The other Apostles were indeed what Peter was, endowed with equal partnership of honor and power, but the beginning proceeds from unity, and primacy is given to Peter, so that one Church of Christ and one chair may be shown. And all are shepherds, and one flock is shown, which is fed by all the Apostles with unanimous consent, so that one Church of Christ may be shown. The Holy Spirit also designates this one Church in the Song of Songs, speaking in the person of the Lord: "My dove is one, my perfect one is one; she is the only one of her mother, chosen by her who bore her" (Song of Songs 6:9). Who does not hold this unity of the Church believes that he holds the faith? Who resists and opposes the Church, who deserts the chair of Peter on which the Church is founded, confides that he is in the Church? When the blessed Apostle Paul also teaches this same thing and shows the sacrament of unity, saying: "One body and one Spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one Baptism, one God" (Ephesians 4:4-6).
